title: Critical tension condition
description: Essential Criteria: The student must state or use that the tension equals the weight of B (T = Mg) when B is about to leave the ground.

title: Centripetal force relation
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly apply Newton's second law to ball A, relating tension to centripetal force (T = m r ω²).

title: Correct angular velocity ω₁
description: Essential Criteria: The final numerical answer for part (1) must be ω₁ = 20 rad/s.

title: Force equilibrium for B
description: Important Criteria: For part (2), the student must set up the vertical force balance for object B (T + N = Mg).

title: Correct normal force
description: Essential Criteria: The final numerical answer for part (2) must be the normal force (or force on ground) = 30 N.

title: Newton's Third Law application
description: Optional Criteria: The student may explicitly state that the force B exerts on the ground equals the normal force from the ground on B.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The solution should maintain consistent units (kg, m, s, N, rad/s) throughout the calculation.

title: Sign/direction error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly writes the force balance as N = Mg + T or misinterprets the direction of forces.

title: Incorrect radius or mass
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student uses the wrong mass (e.g., uses m instead of M for B's weight) or the wrong radius in the centripetal force formula.
